contributions.anchor: the filer's own DONATIONS ledger total, printed 'Sum 7176' (p2), which equals Box B 'Contributions Received this Period' 7,176 on the p4 Summary Page (and Box C, and Box F)
contributions.detail: ⚠ READ THE COMPOSITION BEFORE COMPARING WITH checkrec: this side publishes 12 rows totalling 11,576.00, which is 7,176.00 of CASH (10 rows from the DONATIONS table on p2) PLUS 4,400.00 of IN-KIND (2 rows from the separate IN-KIND table on p3). The reconciliation gates on the CASH figure, which is the scope Box B states. The 10 cash rows sum to 1000+200+100+100+5+280+20+470+1+5000 = 7,176 exactly = the ledger's printed 'Sum' = Box B. BOTH CONVENTIONS WERE TESTED (G1): monetary-only closes exactly at 7,176; monetary-plus-in-kind gives 11,576 against a stated 7,176 and fails by exactly the in-kind sheet's own printed 'Sum 4400'. So this filer keeps in-kind SEPARATE and out of the stated contribution total, and the two in-kind rows are published ALONGSIDE the anchor, flagged in_kind, reproducing their own sheet's printed total to the cent (900 + 3500 = 4,400) — the Paxman precedent. Box C prints the same 7,176 because this is the cycle's first report, so period and year-to-date coincide; it is not summed as an increment.

expenditures.anchor: the filer's own EXPENDITURES ledger total, printed 'Sum 6527.07' (p2), which equals Box D 'Expenditures Made this Period' 6527.07 on the p4 Summary Page
expenditures.detail: 20 rows sum to 3000+725+18.91+116.28+11.97+20.5+200+250+813.36+58.92+272.69+186.62+8.23+23.08+57.6+169.85+422.34+70.78+2.2+98.74 = 6,527.07 exactly = the ledger's printed Sum = Box D. Box E prints the same figure (first report of the cycle) and is never summed as an increment. No expenditure is marked in-kind and the in-kind sheet is a contribution-side list, so monetary-only and monetary-plus-in-kind are identical on this side.

in_kind_convention: IN-KIND KEPT SEPARATE FROM THE STATED TOTAL — monetary-only closes the contribution side. The filer lists in-kind on its OWN sheet (p3, headed IN-KIND, with its own printed 'Sum 4400') and the summary's Box B states only the 7,176 cash figure; adding the in-kind would overshoot Box B by exactly 4,400. Both conventions were tested. The two in-kind rows are published with in_kind=true alongside the cash rows and reproduce their sheet's printed total to the cent. ⚠ Note this is the OPPOSITE convention from the chunk's Tribe filing (5afd8850), where the stated totals INCLUDE the in-kind gift — in-kind treatment is per FILING (G1) and was not carried between filers or between this filer's own two reports.
escalation_note: No disputed cell: the three ledger tables are machine-typed and every figure renders crisply at 900 dpi, and all three printed 'Sum' lines plus Boxes B/C/D/E/F reproduce to the cent. ⚠ THE L1 SIDE-INVERSION SCREEN WAS RUN and came back CLEAN: the sheets are headed DONATIONS (Sum 7176) and EXPENDITURES (Sum 6527.07) and the summary books 7,176 as Box B (contributions) and 6,527.07 as Box D (expenditures) — heading and box agree in sense and scale on both sides, and the content confirms it (named individuals and a PAC on the donations side; retailers, printers, a rodeo and the county elections office on the expenditure side). No side was swapped and nothing was adjudicated. Separately, the filer's own close box reads 649.00 where Box F - Box D = 7,176 - 6,527.07 = 648.93, a 0.07 discrepancy in the filer's arithmetic; it is RECORDED AS PRINTED, touches no itemized row, and was not recomputed.

2.measure_note: pdfinfo: rot 0 on all six pages (checked before measuring). ⚠ THIS PAGE CARRIES TWO SIDE-BY-SIDE OWN-LEDGER TABLES (DONATIONS left, EXPENDITURES right) and prints NO rules at all, so the A2 recovery applies and — per A2's rule that a band measured in one column does not transfer across the sheet — EACH TABLE WAS MEASURED IN ITS OWN COLUMN. This frame is the DONATIONS table only (`cell` = its amount column 29.00-38.50); every EXPENDITURE row instead carries an explicit per-row `geometry` string in the right-hand column, which wins over this frame. `rowbands.py --text-lines --col 28,40` returns 10 bands where 13 printed lines exist (title, 'Amount' header, 10 donation lines, Sum), so THREE amount bands are missing — the L5 limitation, and here it is unmistakably about size: the three dropped amounts are '5', '20' and '1', the shortest figures on the sheet. The gaps are exact multiples of the sheet's 1.68 pitch, so the missing bands interpolate to 39.45, 42.85 and 48.00, and ALL THREE WERE CROP-PROVED at 900 dpi: they rendered '5' (Caleb Smith), '20' (Lauri Updike) and '1' (Bren Smith) respectively. TWO-CROP PROOF of the ends: pct:29.0,32.68,9.5,1.1@p2 rendered '1000' (row 1, John Valentine) and pct:29.0,51.14,9.5,1.1@p2 rendered '5000' (row 10, SAFE PAC). ONE-PAST CONTROL taken at the ledger's own total line, pct:29.0,71.36,9.5,1.1@p2, rendered '7176' — the printed Sum, not an 11th donor. The ledger has TWO BLANK SPACER LINES (before 'Bren Smith 1' and before 'SAFE PAC') which carry nothing and are not indexed.
